There's been captcha solver browser plugins, paywall bypass, and many other tools freely available to circumvent or get around "prove you're human" challenges for awhile now.  
It's a bit Newtonian where there's an action and reaction for those savvy with  the whats what of the internet.  
New ads come out, or tools to obsolete your popup blocker, but, then there's plugins, browser extensions, scripts, and/or updates to things one might already have that pushes back.   For any bother or problem, there's usually a way that comes out to negate, or work around it.  
Similar will apply with various AI employments where we'll eventually get tools that can warn or block against AI via the detection of minute little things and artifacts that would not be present in an actual factual human video.  
It's a constant running battle, and we'll continue to see back and forth with countermeasures against the newer developmental sophistication of certain technologies once we get over the woo woo excitement about AI and start working on marketable ways to detect it with some software, and possibly software that can make money for the developer.   Money fuels development, and when devs figure out they can get paid to counter AI, we'll begin to see those counter apps.
